rulebook: Chapter 110-300 WAC, Foundational Quality Standards for Early Learning Programs (Last Update: 7/1/26)

items.requirement: The center must have a written nondiscrimination policy addressing the protected factors listed in the rule.
items.quote: An early learning program must have a written nondiscrimination policy addressing at least the factors listed in subsection (1) of this section.

items.requirement: The center must inform parents or guardians about the importance of developmental screenings for children birth through age five.
items.quote: An early learning provider must inform parents or guardians about the importance of developmental screenings for each child from birth through age five.

items.requirement: At least once per calendar year, the center must supply parents or guardians kindergarten or school readiness materials when developmentally appropriate.
items.quote: At least once per calendar year, an early learning provider must supply to parents or guardians kindergarten or school readiness materials when developmentally appropriate for enrolled children.

items.requirement: If screen time is offered, it must be educational and age appropriate, must not occur during meals or snacks, and must not exceed two and one-half hours per week for children over 24 months through preschool in full-day care.
items.quote: Total screen time must not exceed two and one-half hours per week for each child over twenty-four months of age through preschool in full-day care (one and one-quarter hours per child in half-day care).

items.requirement: Firearms, guns, weapons, and ammunition must not be on the premises of a center early learning program.
items.quote: Ensuring firearms, guns, weapons, and ammunition are not on the premises of a center early learning program.

items.requirement: Meals and snacks must be served not less than two hours and not more than three hours apart unless the child is asleep, with required numbers based on hours in care.
items.quote: Meals and snacks must be served not less than two hours and not more than three hours apart unless the child is asleep;

items.requirement: Meals, snacks, and beverages must comply with current USDA CACFP or National School Lunch and School Breakfast Program standards, and menus must be dated.
items.quote: Meals, snack foods, and beverages provided to children in care must comply with the requirements contained in the most current edition of the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) standards, or the USDA National School Lunch and School Breakfast Program standards.

items.requirement: For a child with a known food allergy or special dietary requirement, the center must obtain written instructions in an individual care plan from the child's health care provider and parent or guardian.
items.quote: An early learning provider must obtain written instructions (the individual care plan) from the child's health care provider and parent or guardian when caring for a child with a known food allergy or special dietary requirement due to a health condition.

items.requirement: A written food plan must be developed by the provider and parent or guardian, signed by all parties, and followed when accommodating special feeding needs, diets, preferences, or other needs.
items.quote: A written food plan must be developed by the provider and a child's parent or guardian, signed by all parties, and followed when accommodating a child's: (a) Special feeding needs;

items.requirement: If a parent provides meals, the center must notify the parent in writing of USDA CACFP requirements and supplement meals that do not satisfy them if necessary.
items.quote: If a parent or guardian provides meals for their child, an early learning provider must: (a) Notify the parent or guardian in writing of the USDA CACFP requirements for each meal; and (b) Supplement a child's meal that does not satisfy USDA CACFP requirements if necessary.

items.requirement: An ill child must be sent home or reasonably separated if the illness prevents normal participation, requires more care than staff can give, risks others, or may spread.
items.quote: An ill child must be sent home or reasonably separated from other children if: (a) The illness or condition prevents the child from participating in normal activities;

items.requirement: A child must be excluded for specified symptoms such as fever with behavior change, repeated vomiting, diarrhea, rash, open sores, lice, ringworm, scabies, or appearing severely ill.
items.quote: Unless covered by an individual care plan or protected by the ADA, an ill child, staff member, or other individual must be sent home or isolated from children in care if the ill individual has:

items.requirement: Within 24 hours of learning of a diagnosed contagious disease, the center must provide written notice to the department, local health jurisdiction, and parents or guardians.
items.quote: At the first opportunity, but in no case longer than twenty-four hours of learning that an enrolled child, staff member, volunteer, or household member has been diagnosed by a health care professional with a contagious disease pursuant to WAC 246-110-010(3), as now and hereafter amended, an early learning provider must provide written notice to the department, the local health jurisdiction, and the parents or guardians of the enrolled children.

items.requirement: Parents or guardians must provide proof of vaccination or acquired immunity on or before the child's first day, and providers must receive current immunization records upon enrollment and annually thereafter.
items.quote: On or before their children's first day of attending an early learning program, the parents or guardians of enrolled children must give to early learning providers proof of vaccination or acquired immunity for the vaccine-preventable disease, required under RCW 43.216.690 and chapter 246-105 WAC.

items.requirement: Providers must exclude a child from care according to the criteria in WAC 246-105-080 and may exclude exempt children during an outbreak of a vaccine-preventable disease.
items.quote: Early learning providers must exclude a child from care according to the criteria listed in WAC 246-105-080.

items.requirement: Medication must not be given without written and signed consent from the parent or guardian, and must be administered according to the label directions.
items.quote: An early learning provider must not give medication to any child without written and signed consent from that child's parent or guardian, must administer medication pursuant to directions on the medication label, and using appropriate cleaned and sanitized medication measuring devices.

items.requirement: Staff must not give medication unless they have completed required medication training and competency assessment.
items.quote: An early learning provider must not give medication to a child if the provider has not successfully completed: (a) An orientation about the early learning program's medication policies and procedures; (b) The department standardized training course in medication administration that includes a competency assessment pursuant to WAC 110-300-0106(10) or equivalent training;

items.requirement: If pets or animals are kept on the premises, the center must have and follow a pet and animal policy and provide written notice to parents and guardians.
items.quote: If an early learning provider keeps pets or animals on the early learning program premises: (a) The provider must have and follow a pet and animal policy; and (b) Provide written notice to children's parents and guardians.

items.requirement: The center must have a pest control policy and notify parents or guardians at least 48 hours before pesticide application, unless an emergency.
items.quote: If pesticides are used, the early learning provider must notify the parents or guardians of enrolled children what pesticide will be applied and where it will be applied no less than forty-eight hours before application, unless in cases of emergency (such as a wasp nest).

items.requirement: A supervised daily rest period must be offered for children preschool age and younger who remain in care more than six hours per day or show a need for rest.
items.quote: An early learning provider must offer a supervised daily rest period for children preschool age and younger who remain in care for more than six hours per day, or who show a need for rest.

items.requirement: Overnight care between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m. requires department approval when any enrolled child sleeps three or more hours at the program.
items.quote: An early learning provider must be approved by the department to provide overnight care between nine o'clock at night and five o'clock in the morning when any enrolled child sleeps for three or more hours at the program.

items.requirement: Infants must be placed on their backs to sleep, actively supervised with visible checks every 15 minutes, and cribs must not contain blankets, toys, pillows, or bumpers.
items.quote: Placing an infant to sleep on their back or following the current standard of American Academy of Pediatrics. If an infant turns over while sleeping, the provider must return the infant to their back until the infant is able to independently roll from back to front and front to back;

items.requirement: After a safe sleep violation, the center must post the notice for two weeks or until corrected and provide parents a letter and safe sleep information within five business days.
items.quote: Within five business days of receiving notice of the violation, provide all parents and guardians of enrolled children with: (i) A letter describing the safe sleep violation; and (ii) Written information on safe sleep practices for infants.

items.requirement: The center must develop an individual care plan for each child with special needs and notify the department when such a child is enrolled or identified.
items.quote: An early learning provider must develop an individual care plan for each child with special needs and must notify the department when a child with special needs is enrolled or identified in the early learning program.

items.requirement: Staff must not use prohibited discipline such as spanking, hitting, shaming, humiliation, or other listed harmful practices.
items.quote: An early learning provider, staff member, or household member is prohibited from using the following behaviors and discipline of children:

items.requirement: Physical restraint may only be used when a child's safety or others' safety is threatened, must be gentle and minimal, and must be reported and documented.
items.quote: Physical restraint must only be used if a child's safety or the safety of others is threatened and must be: (a) Limited to holding a child as gently as possible to accomplish restraint;

items.requirement: A child may be expelled only for serious safety concerns that cannot be reduced or eliminated through reasonable modifications.
items.quote: An early learning provider may expel a child only if: (a) The child exhibits behavior that presents a serious safety concern for that child or others; and (b) The program is not able to reduce or eliminate the safety concern through reasonable modifications.

items.requirement: Only a child's parent or guardian, authorized staff, government representatives with verifiable authority, or a person authorized in writing or by phone by the parent may have unsupervised access to a child in care.
items.quote: An early learning provider must only allow the following persons to have unsupervised access to a child in care: (a) That child's own parent or guardian;

items.requirement: Staff must supervise children by scanning, visibly checking, positioning themselves to see all areas, and being available to assist or redirect children.
items.quote: An early learning provider must supervise children in care by: (a) Scanning the environment looking and listening for both verbal and nonverbal cues to anticipate problems and plan accordingly;

items.requirement: During water activities, the center must meet the supervision requirements, including 1:1 ratio for infants and keeping toddlers within arm's length.
items.quote: During water activities, an early learning provider must: (a) Ensure a one-to-one (1:1) staff-to-child ratio for infants; (b) Hold or have continuous touch of infants, nonambulatory toddlers, and children with special needs as required; and (c) Keep toddlers within arm's length.

items.requirement: Center classrooms must meet the maximum group sizes and staff-to-child ratios for each age group.
items.quote: In each classroom or well-defined space, the maximum group size and ratio of center staff members to children, including children related to staff or the licensee, must be:

items.requirement: The center must have an established program and daily schedule that includes active outdoor play time, scheduled meals, rest periods, and other applicable routines.
items.quote: An early learning provider must have an established program and daily schedule that is familiar to children.

items.requirement: The parent handbook must include a family engagement and partnership communication plan.
items.quote: A family engagement and partnership communication plan;

items.requirement: The center must obtain a parent or guardian's permission for photography, videotaping, or surveillance of their child.
items.quote: A parent or guardian's permission for photography, videotaping, or surveillance of their child;

items.requirement: The handbook must state the center's alcohol, tobacco, cannabis use and prohibition of illegal drugs policy.
items.quote: Alcohol, tobacco, cannabis use and prohibition of illegal drugs;

items.requirement: The handbook must include the center's curriculum philosophy on how children learn and develop and how it is implemented.
items.quote: Curriculum philosophy on how children learn and develop, and how this philosophy is implemented;

items.requirement: The handbook must include a child guidance plan that includes restraint policies and forbids corporal punishment.
items.quote: Child guidance plan, which includes restraint policies and forbidding corporal punishment;

items.requirement: The handbook must state staff-to-child ratios and classroom types offered, if applicable.
items.quote: Early learning program staff-to-child ratios and classroom types offered, if applicable;

items.requirement: If the center cares for children with specific or special needs, the handbook must include a policy for that care.
items.quote: Care for children with specific or special needs;

items.requirement: If infant or toddler care is offered, the handbook must include policies covering diapering, feeding, toilet training, child sleep pattern, and safe sleep requirements.
items.quote: Infant and toddler care, covering: (A) Diapering; (B) Feeding; (C) Toilet training; (D) Child sleep pattern; and (E) Safe sleep requirements.

items.requirement: If religious or cultural activities are offered, the handbook must include a policy including how holidays will be celebrated.
items.quote: Religious and cultural activities, including how holidays will be celebrated;

items.requirement: The handbook must explain how weapons on the premises are secured.
items.quote: How weapons on the premises are secured.

items.requirement: The handbook must state program days and hours of operation, including closure dates and observed holidays.
items.quote: Program days and hours of operation, including closure dates and observed holidays;

items.requirement: The handbook must explain what information is required for the child's record and how it is kept current and confidential.
items.quote: Information required for the child's record, including: (i) The importance and plan for keeping the information current; (ii) A plan to keep the child's information confidential; and (iii) Who may legally access the child's information.

items.requirement: If applicable, the handbook must include a kindergarten transition plan.
items.quote: A kindergarten transition plan, if applicable;

items.requirement: The handbook must state what parents or guardians must supply for their child, such as extra clothing or diapers.
items.quote: What parents or guardians must supply for their child (for example: Extra clothing or diapers);

items.requirement: The handbook must state permission for a parent or guardian's access to areas of the early learning program during business hours.
items.quote: Permission for a parent or guardian's access to areas of the early learning program during business hours;

items.requirement: The handbook must state the provider and staff's duty to report incidents, including reporting suspected abuse or neglect of a child or youth.
items.quote: The early learning provider and program staff's duty to report incidents including reporting suspected abuse or neglect of a child or youth;

items.requirement: If mixed age groups are used, the handbook must include a policy for them, including when children may be in a mixed age group.
items.quote: Policies regarding mixed age groups, if applicable (including when children may be in a mixed age group);

items.requirement: A child may be kept in care up to a maximum of ten hours each day, with limited extensions based on parent work, agreed schedule, or travel.
items.quote: An early learning provider may keep a child in care up to a maximum of ten hours each day. If needed, the maximum time may be extended based upon the parent or guardian's work, an agreed upon alternate schedule, or travel to and from the early learning program.

items.requirement: Daily attendance records must document each child's name, date of care, arrival and departure times, and parent or authorized person signature.
items.quote: These records must clearly document: (a) The name of the child; (b) The date of care; (c) Child arrival and departure times from the early learning program; (d) Signature or electronic signature of parent, guardian or other authorized person at the time of arrival and departure;

items.requirement: A child's parent or guardian must be allowed access to all of their own child's records.
items.quote: A child's parent or guardian must be allowed access to all of their own child's records.

items.requirement: The emergency preparedness plan must be reviewed with parents or guardians when a child is enrolled and when the plan is updated.
items.quote: Be reviewed with parents or guardians when a child is enrolled and when the plan is updated.

items.requirement: The center must practice and record fire and evacuation drills monthly and earthquake, lockdown, or shelter-in-place drills every three months.
items.quote: Fire and evacuation drill once each calendar month; (b) Earthquake, lockdown, or shelter-in-place drill once every three calendar months;

items.requirement: When there is reasonable cause to believe a child has suffered abuse or neglect, the provider must report it to law enforcement or the department.
items.quote: Pursuant to RCW 26.44.030, when an early learning provider has reasonable cause to believe that a child has suffered abuse or neglect, that provider must report such incident, or cause a report to be made, to the proper law enforcement agency or the department.

items.requirement: Serious injuries and situations requiring emergency response must be reported to parents or guardians and the department within required time frames, with written incident reports submitted within 24 hours.
items.quote: In addition to reporting to the department by phone or email, an early learning provider must submit a written incident report of the following on a department form within 24 hours:

items.requirement: The provider must immediately report a child's death, serious injury, need for emergency or poison services, or an incident reported to health authorities to the parent or guardian.
items.quote: An early learning provider must immediately report to the parent or guardian: (a) Their child's death, serious injury, need for emergency or poison services; or (b) An incident involving their child that was reported to the local health jurisdiction or the department of health.

items.requirement: During travel to an off-site activity, the center must maintain ratios, active supervision, first-aid/CPR certification, attendance checks, and never leave children unattended in a vehicle.
items.quote: During travel to an off-site activity, an early learning provider must: (a) Have the health history, appropriate medication (if applicable), emergency information, and emergency medical authorization forms accessible for each child being transported;

items.requirement: Services may be terminated due to a parent or guardian's inability to meet program expectations and requirements, such as unpaid bills, continual late arrivals, or inappropriate or unsafe behavior.
items.quote: An early learning provider may terminate a child's services due to that child's parent or guardian's inability to meet the expectations and requirements of the early learning program.

items.requirement: The center must have and follow a child restraint policy, and only trained staff may restrain a child in accordance with the rule.
items.quote: An early learning provider must have and follow a child restraint policy that contains behavior management and practices, pursuant to WAC 110-300-0335.

items.requirement: The center must have and follow a written health policy reviewed and approved by the department.
items.quote: An early learning provider must have and follow a written health policy reviewed and approved by the department that includes the topics listed in subsection (2) of this section.

items.requirement: The health policy must include medication management, storage, administration, and documentation.
items.quote: Medication management, storage, administration and documentation;

items.requirement: The center must have and follow a policy that promotes consistent care of children.
items.quote: An early learning program must have and follow a policy that promotes the consistent care of children.

dropped_unverified.requirement: The center must have and follow an expulsion policy and include it in the handbook.
If dual language learning is offered, the handbook must include a policy for it.
If transportation or off-site field trips are offered, the handbook must include a policy for them.
If water activities are offered, the handbook must include a policy for them.
If overnight care is offered, the handbook must include a policy for it.
The handbook must state enrollment and disenrollment requirements.
The handbook must state fees and payment plans.
The handbook must state sign-in and sign-out requirements.
The handbook must include the center's termination of services policy.
The handbook must include the center's emergency preparedness plan.

The handbook must describe where parents or guardians may find and review the health policy, staff policies, consistent care policy, menus, liability insurance, inspection reports, enforcement notices, and other relevant policies.
dropped_unverified.quote: Description of where the parent or guardian may find and review the early learning program's: (i) Health policy; (ii) Staff policies, if applicable; (iii) Consistent care policy; (iv) Menus; (v) Liability insurance; (vi) Inspection reports and notices of enforcement actions, if applicable; and (vii) Other relevant program policies.

dropped_unverified.requirement: Each enrolled child's record must have signed documentation stating the parent or guardian reviewed the handbook and early learning program policies.
dropped_unverified.quote: Each enrolled child's record must have signed documentation stating the parent or guardian reviewed the handbook and early learning program policies.
